payload.prfaq:
PRESS RELEASE - "Closing an iteration now leaves trunk clean and the record intact." As of i5d, an iteration commits at each blessed milestone onto its own branch, and closing it merges only live claims into trunk. The design nodes, requirements, tests and product code land where every future iteration reads them. The evidence, gate records and machine state stay on the branch, named by a mandatory iter/<id> tag, reachable forever and absent from every checkout of trunk. A close that would produce nothing now refuses instead of reporting success.

HOSTILE FAQ.
Q: You are deleting my evidence. A: No. The merge keeps both parents, so the branch tip stays in the history, and a tag is created BEFORE the filtered commit so it has a permanent name. git show iter/<id>:<path> returns any of it. The close refuses if the tag cannot be created.
Q: What if the filtered merge hits a conflict? A: It stops and aborts, exactly as today. A conflict means two lines changed the same live claim, which is a human question, not something to resolve by dropping paths.
Q: You are inventing a git trick. Will git cope later? A: The trick is ordinary - merge without committing, adjust the index, commit. Git records it as a normal two-parent merge. It is nevertheless unproven HERE, which is why M6 spikes it rather than assuming it.
Q: Why not squash? A: A squash sheds the second parent, and with it the only structural link to the record. The tag would then be the sole thread, and one deleted tag would orphan an iteration's whole history.
Q: The agent commits without me. Is that a new authority? A: No. Commits already ride the bless window; only the target changes, from trunk to the iteration's own branch. Trunk still changes exactly once per iteration, at the close.
Q: WHAT DOES THE BOARD SHOW AFTER A CLOSE? A: This one did not answer cleanly - see below.
Q: What if I want the old behaviour? A: Then you are asking for evidence on trunk, which is what the design forbids; the escape is to read it from the tag, not to re-merge it.
payload.findings_folded: ONE finding, folded into scope. The board question exposed a regression this iteration would otherwise ship: projectState discovers iterations by listing directories under spec/iterations on disk, so the moment a close removes a closed iteration's files from trunk, that iteration would vanish from the board entirely - not merely lose its detail. Reading the detail from git is i5e's job and stays out of scope, but DISAPPEARING is a regression, not a deferral. Folded in: closed iterations must remain listable after the filtered close, sourced from the grant index on trunk, which already names every iteration and every gate it passed. This also strengthens the owner's ruling that the thin grant index stays on trunk - it is precisely what keeps the archive discoverable once the heavy material leaves. Scope gains one line; the i5e boundary is unchanged. Nothing else in the packet moved: R1 already required the tag before the filter, and the conflict path was already specified to abort.
